meta.subtitle: Nuclear-anchored clean-power generator leveraged to AI data-center demand, digesting the $21.8 billion Calpine acquisition

analystCommentary: We rate Constellation Energy (CEG) BUY with a $290-$350 target range against a $263.46 price as of September 22, 2026. The company is a nuclear-anchored clean-energy generator; its 10-Q for the period ended June 30, 2026 describes a fleet of 55 gigawatts, and the company is described as the largest nuclear energy company in the U.S. The bull case is straightforward: AI-driven data-center power demand is converting into long-term contracts, including 920 MW of new nuclear PPAs beginning 2029 through 2032 and 380 MW-plus of CyrusOne agreements at the Freestone Energy Center. FY25 revenue grew {+ +19.5% +} to $22.7B, and consensus sees FY26E revenue of $35.1B, a {+ +55% +} step-up driven by the January 2026 Calpine acquisition. Shares trade at 25.7x trailing and 21.7x NTM earnings, a premium to a typical regulated utility that reflects merchant-power and demand-growth optionality. The counter-case is real. Earnings and cash flows vary with power and fuel prices; GAAP net income attributable to common shareholders fell to $513 million in the second quarter of 2026 from $839 million a year earlier, a {- -$326 million -} move even as the six-month figure rose. The stock already sits well off its 52-week high. Our base case is $300 (+14%), our bear is $205 (about -22%), and the reward/risk near 0.6x supports a BUY below the Street's $348.55 consensus target.

executiveSummary.companyOverview: Constellation Energy Corporation is a competitive power producer and retail supplier headquartered in Baltimore, Maryland. Its 10-Q for the period ended June 30, 2026 describes a fleet of 55 gigawatts spanning nuclear, natural gas, oil, geothermal, hydro, wind and solar, with the generating capacity to power the equivalent of 27 million homes and to supply about 10% of the nation's clean energy. The company is described as the largest nuclear energy company in the U.S. and as a leading competitive retail supplier serving approximately 2.5 million customer accounts, including 80% of the Fortune 100. On January 7, 2026 the company acquired Calpine Corporation for a purchase price of approximately $21.8 billion, funded with 50 million newly issued shares and approximately $4.5 billion in cash; Calpine adds roughly 23 GWs of predominantly natural gas, geothermal, battery storage and solar capacity plus a retail platform serving about 62 TWhs of load annually. That fleet figure exceeds the roughly 31,676 megawatts in the vendor's company description, which predates the Calpine close. The company reports as a single reportable segment, shown here as a consolidated total; FY25 revenue was $22.7B.

thesis.body: Constellation is a nuclear-anchored baseload generator positioned for structural growth in electricity demand from data centers, with a lengthening book of long-term power purchase agreements to match. FY25 revenue rose {+ +19.5% +} to $22.7B, and consensus FY26E revenue of $35.1B embeds the Calpine acquisition. The offset is commodity exposure: the company's own risk factors state that earnings and cash flows are exposed to spot and forward power prices, and baseload nuclear can face negative pricing in oversupplied hours. At 25.7x trailing and 21.7x NTM earnings, and roughly 36% below the 52-week high of $412.70, the shares price in continued execution but no longer price in the peak. We see a base case of $300, a genuine bear near $205, and a reward/risk that supports a BUY at a discount to the Street's $348.55 consensus target.

catalysts: Closing of the Calpine integration and the associated LS Power divestitures, valued at $5.0 billion for about 4.4 GWs in PJM and $860 million for the 606 MW Brazos Valley Energy Center, both expected by the end of 2026.

Conversion of AI and data-center demand into signed contracts, following 920 MW of new long-term nuclear PPAs for 2029 through 2032 and the 380 MW plus a 380 MW Phase 2 CyrusOne agreements at the Freestone Energy Center.
PJM capacity outcomes: the 2028/2029 Base Residual Auction cleared at the $325/MW-day price cap in July 2026, with subsequent auctions bounded by the $175 to $325 collar.
New capacity reaching commercial operation, including the 460 MW Pin Oak Creek Energy Center in April 2026 and the 105 MW Pastoria Solar Project with its 80 MW/320 MWh Power Bank online in July 2026.
Delivery against consensus FY27E revenue of $36.4B, with EPS of $12.13 (FY26E) and $13.25 (FY27E), that frame the growth outlook.
risks: Commodity-price exposure across power and fuel; see Risks.
Calpine integration and dividend risk; see Risks.
PJM and FERC market-design uncertainty; see Risks.
Nuclear fuel supply under Russia-related sanctions; see Risks.
Valuation: a premium multiple and a 0.65% dividend yield leave limited cushion if growth disappoints.

financials.incomeCommentary: FY25 revenue was $22.7B, up {+ +19.5% +} year over year, after a volatile stretch of +25.0% in FY22, -3.4% in FY23 and -9.0% in FY24 that reflects the swing in wholesale power prices. FY25 net income was $2.3B and diluted EPS was $7.40, down from $11.89 in FY24. Operating margin fell to 13.6% in FY25 from 22.9% in FY24, and EBITDA declined to $5.7B from $7.1B. In the second quarter of 2026, revenue was $5.8B, up {+ +13% +} year over year, at a 9.9% operating margin. GAAP net income attributable to common shareholders was $513 million in the second quarter of 2026 versus $839 million a year earlier, a {- -$326 million -} decline; over the six months ended June 30, 2026 the same measure was $2,103 million versus $957 million, an increase of {+ +$1,146 million +}. The six-month gain alongside a lower quarter reflects items around the Calpine close rather than a clean run-rate. Consensus FY26E revenue of $35.1B implies a {+ +55% +} step-up as Calpine consolidates.
financials.balanceCommentary: At FY25 year-end the company carried $9.0B of total debt against $3.6B of cash, for net debt of $5.4B, unchanged from FY24. Total equity was $14.9B and the current ratio was 1.53. On a trailing basis net debt to EBITDA was 2.9x, interest coverage was 5.9x, and the current ratio was 1.46. These annual balance-sheet figures predate the January 7, 2026 Calpine close, which added approximately $21.8 billion of consideration, including approximately $4.5 billion in cash and 50 million newly issued shares; post-close leverage and share count therefore differ from the FY25 columns and are not captured in this grounding set. The offsetting divestitures to LS Power, valued at $5.0 billion and $860 million, are intended to satisfy regulatory commitments and, on closing, would return cash against that consideration.
financials.cashflowCommentary: FY25 operating cash flow was $4.2B, a swing to positive after four consecutive years of outflows that reached as much as $5.3B in FY23, reflecting collateral and working-capital swings in a hedging-intensive generation and trading business. FY25 capital expenditure was $2.9B, and free cash flow was $1.3B at a 5.7% FCF margin, positive after four negative years. On a trailing basis the FCF yield is a thin 0.3%. Share repurchases stepped down to $0.4B in FY25 from $1.0B in each of FY23 and FY24, while dividends paid were $0.5B against a 0.65% yield. That free cash flow only modestly exceeds the dividend, leaving limited internal funding for the capital program and the Calpine-related outlays.

valuation.multiplesCommentary: On the company column, CEG trades at 25.7x trailing earnings, 3.8x sales and 14.2x EV/EBITDA, with a forward P/E of 21.7x on next-twelve-month estimates and about 19.9x on FY27E EPS of $13.25. That is a premium to a typical regulated utility, consistent with a merchant generator whose output carries demand-growth and AI-power optionality rather than a fixed regulated return. The Street is constructive: 22 analysts rate the stock Buy 19, Hold 3, Sell 0, with a consensus target of $348.55 (+32.3%), a median of $350.50 and a range of $290.00 to $441.00. A comparable peer set and peer multiples are not on the grounding surface, so a formal peer comparison is pending a peer data source. We therefore anchor valuation on the company's own multiples and forward estimates rather than on a peer premium or discount.

scenarios.name: Bull
scenarios.driver: AI and data-center demand converts into signed long-term PPAs beyond the 920 MW of nuclear PPAs for 2029 through 2032 and the CyrusOne agreements at Freestone; PJM capacity clears at the $325/MW-day cap into the 2029/2030 auction; Calpine integrates without earnings dilution and power prices stay firm, re-rating the shares toward the Street's high target of $441.00 on FY27E EPS of $13.25.

scenarios.name: Base
scenarios.driver: Calpine integration proceeds on plan and the July 2026 clearing of the 2028/2029 PJM auction at the price cap supports capacity earnings; consensus revenue of $35.1B in FY26E and $36.4B in FY27E and FY26E EPS of $12.13 is broadly met; the shares hold a premium generator multiple below last year's high.

scenarios.name: Bear
scenarios.driver: Power prices normalize and PJM capacity retreats toward the $175/MW-day floor after the collared auctions; Calpine integration proves costly and dilutive as the 10-K risk factors warn; the FY26E revenue step-up disappoints as the $5.0 billion and $860 million LS Power divestitures close, compressing the multiple toward the mid-teens.

valuation.scenarioCommentary: We weight the Base case at 50% and the Bull and Bear at 25% each, giving a probability-weighted fair value of about $299, an expected upside of roughly +13% and a bear-case downside of about -22%. The resulting reward/risk near 0.6x clears the threshold for a BUY while stopping short of a stronger call. The bear at $205 is a real scenario, not a formality: it sits about 22% below the current price and rests on power-price normalization, a costly Calpine integration and a multiple that de-rates toward the mid-teens. Our target range of $290 to $350 brackets the base case and sits below the Street's consensus target, reflecting the commodity sensitivity and integration risk that temper an otherwise constructive demand story. A move above the range would require the Bull-case combination of firm power prices, capacity clearing at the cap and dilution-free integration.

segments.name: Consolidated
segments.body: The company reports as a single reportable segment, so revenue is shown here as one consolidated total of $22.7B for FY25 rather than a product or regional split. Operationally the fleet spans nuclear, natural gas, oil, geothermal, hydro, wind and solar totaling 55 gigawatts per the 10-Q, with activity concentrated in the PJM, ERCOT and California markets referenced in the filing: the Freestone and Pin Oak Creek assets serve ERCOT, while in California the Pastoria Solar Project is contracted by the California Department of Water Resources and the co-located Pastoria Power Bank carries a 15-year power purchase agreement with Pacific Gas and Electric Company. The consolidated presentation reflects an integrated generation and competitive retail model that serves approximately 2.5 million customer accounts, including 80% of the Fortune 100. Because the company discloses no segment revenue breakout, we do not quote a regional or fuel-type revenue mix.

moatFactors.name: Irreplaceable nuclear fleet
moatFactors.body: The company is described as the largest nuclear energy company in the U.S., within a fleet that supplies about 10% of the nation's clean energy and can power the equivalent of 27 million homes. Nuclear capacity of this scale is difficult to replicate given licensing, siting and capital barriers, and it provides around-the-clock baseload output that intermittent resources cannot match.

moatFactors.name: Long-term contracted cash flows
moatFactors.body: The company has signed 920 MW of long-term nuclear PPAs of 15 to 20 years beginning 2029 through 2032 with investment-grade customers, including a 176 MW agreement with Walmart that enables a 30 MW expansion at the Dresden Clean Energy Center. Data-center agreements with CyrusOne at Freestone and a 15-year PG&E contract for the Pastoria Power Bank extend the contracted book and dampen merchant price exposure over time.

moatFactors.name: Retail scale and customer base
moatFactors.body: The retail franchise described under the consolidated segment above spans a broad customer base, and the Calpine platform adds about 62 TWhs of retail load annually. Retail scale supports hedging of generation output, though the 10-K notes retail margins and volumes face active competition and depend on continued state support for retail choice.

moatFactors.name: Commodity price exposure
moatFactors.body: The 10-K states that earnings and cash flows are exposed to spot and forward power and fuel prices, that baseload nuclear can face negative pricing in oversupplied hours, and that hedges can be ineffective. This commodity sensitivity caps the durable pricing power that a wide-moat rating would require, which is why we rate the moat narrow rather than wide.

businessMoat.durability: The durable core is the licensed nuclear fleet, which combines high barriers to entry with a demand backdrop that increasingly values firm, clean baseload power. That advantage is real but not unconditional. Merchant output is repriced with the market, so the value of the fleet rises and falls with power prices and PJM capacity outcomes, and the 10-K is explicit that results are exposed to price volatility and to market-design changes with little notice. The lengthening book of long-term PPAs is the mechanism that could widen the moat by converting merchant exposure into contracted cash flow, but those contracts begin in 2029 and beyond, so the near-term earnings stream remains commodity-linked. We judge the moat narrow and improving rather than wide.

points: The January 2026 Calpine acquisition adds roughly 23 GWs of natural gas, geothermal, battery and solar capacity and about 62 TWhs of annual retail load, and underpins the consensus FY26E revenue of $35.1B, a {+ +55% +} step-up over FY25.

AI and data-center demand is being contracted directly: the CyrusOne agreements at the Freestone Energy Center total 380 MW plus a 380 MW Phase 2, alongside 400 MW of Calpine-CyrusOne agreements at the Thad Hill Energy Center.

The company signed 920 MW of long-term nuclear PPAs of 15 to 20 years beginning 2029 through 2032, including the 176 MW Walmart agreement that enables a 30 MW capacity expansion at the Dresden Clean Energy Center.

New build is reaching service, including the 460 MW Pin Oak Creek Energy Center in April 2026 and the 105 MW Pastoria Solar Project with an 80 MW/320 MWh Power Bank online in July 2026 under a 15-year PG&E PPA.
PJM capacity pricing supports the outlook near term: the 2028/2029 Base Residual Auction cleared at the $325/MW-day cap in July 2026, with all submitted CEG units clearing.

The counter-case is that this growth is capital-intensive and contingent: FY25 capital expenditure was $2.9B, the near-term PPAs do not begin until 2029, and the $5.0 billion and $860 million divestitures reduce the asset base as they close.

management.leadership: The proxy statement's Summary Compensation Table identifies five named executive officers, listed by surname as Dominguez, Eggers, Hanson, Barron and McHugh; the proxy excerpt does not state their individual titles, so we do not assign roles beyond what the filing shows. The company states that the CEO's compensation is developed and administered by the Compensation Committee and approved by the independent members of the Board. In its Compensation Discussion and Analysis, the company reports that its total shareholder return since becoming an independent public company in 2022 has outperformed both the S&P 500 and its peer group, a claim we attribute to management rather than verify independently. The most concrete near-term test of leadership is execution on the Calpine integration and the related divestitures.
management.capitalAllocation: Capital allocation has shifted toward acquisition-led growth. In FY25 the company spent $2.9B on capital expenditure, repurchased $0.4B of stock, down from $1.0B in each of FY23 and FY24, and paid $0.5B in dividends against a 0.65% yield. The January 2026 Calpine acquisition, at approximately $21.8 billion funded with 50 million new shares and approximately $4.5 billion in cash, dwarfs those returns and signals a preference for scale and diversification over buybacks. The 10-K cautions there is no assurance of the dividend at the current rate after the acquisition, and FY25 free cash flow of $1.3B only modestly exceeds the dividend, so the balance between growth investment, deleveraging and shareholder returns is a live question that the pending $5.0 billion and $860 million divestitures are meant to help resolve.
management.governance: The Board has affirmatively determined that none of the non-employee directors who served in 2025, nor any nominee, has a material relationship with the company, and that each is independent under the Nasdaq and SEC standards in the Corporate Governance Principles. All members of the Audit & Risk Committee and of the Compensation Committee are independent under the applicable standards. The proxy describes pay-for-performance practices: a majority of NEO pay is variable cash and equity, incentive awards are capped and subject to clawback, change-in-control benefits use double-trigger vesting, and there are no employment agreements with the CEO or NEOs, no hedging or pledging of company stock, and no option repricing without stockholder approval. The company reports no related-person transactions identified in 2025. For a minority holder we read this profile as a governance mitigant rather than a concern: full board and committee independence, paired with capped, clawback-subject and double-trigger pay weighted toward variable cash and equity, tempers agency risk at a moment when management is executing a large, dilutive acquisition and has flagged possible pressure on the dividend.
management.insiderOwnership: Insider ownership is low. Directors and executive officers as a group of 21 individuals held 1,140,643 shares as of March 2, 2026, which the proxy states is less than 1% of the shares outstanding; the individual holdings shown are led by a non-employee director (Lawless, 161,967 shares) and a named executive officer (Dominguez, 157,074 shares). The proxy's list of holders above 5% mixes filing vintages rather than a single current snapshot: The Vanguard Group at 11.7% and BlackRock at 7.2% are drawn from Schedule 13G/A filings as of December 29, 2023, whereas ECP ControlCo's 7.0% comes from a Schedule 13G filed January 14, 2026, with State Street (5.7%) and Capital International Investors (5.5%) also listed. The modest insider stake means alignment rests more on the stock-ownership requirements and incentive design described in the proxy than on large direct holdings.

idiosyncratic: Calpine integration and dilution: the approximately $21.8 billion acquisition carries what the 10-K describes as a complex, costly and time-consuming integration with potential unknown liabilities, reduced voting power for existing shareholders, EPS dilution, and no assurance of the dividend at the current rate.

Power and fuel price exposure: the 10-K states earnings and cash flows are exposed to spot and forward power prices and to fuel costs, and that baseload nuclear plants can face negative pricing when supply exceeds demand; risk-management hedges can also prove ineffective.

PJM and FERC market design: capacity revenue depends on a price collar of roughly $175 to $325/MW-day and on FERC's co-location and Show Cause rulings, and the 10-K warns that market-rule changes can adversely affect the business with little notice.

Nuclear fuel supply: the company relies on long-term uranium contracts and has increased inventory to manage sanctions tied to the Russia and Ukraine conflict and the Prohibiting Russian Uranium Imports Act, but non-performance by suppliers could materially affect operations.

State environmental policy: the Illinois Climate and Equitable Jobs Act sets a January 1, 2030 CO2 deadline for certain gas units subject to reliability exceptions, and California's Cap-and-Invest Program adds compliance obligations for covered plants.
risks.systemic: As a capital-intensive generator that has just funded a large acquisition partly with cash, CEG is sensitive to interest rates and to access to capital markets, both cited in the 10-K risk factors. Its output is tied to the broader power-demand cycle, which depends on economic activity and on the pace of data-center buildout, and to natural gas prices, which set the marginal cost of power in many hours. As a stock carrying a growth premium, it is also exposed to multiple compression if sentiment around AI-driven power demand cools; the shares already trade well below their 52-week high, which shows how quickly that premium can move.

body: We rate Constellation Energy BUY with a target range of $290 to $350 against a $263.46 price. The company is a nuclear-anchored clean-energy generator with genuine optionality on AI and data-center power demand, a lengthening book of long-term PPAs, and a newly enlarged fleet of 55 gigawatts following the Calpine acquisition. At 21.7x NTM earnings and still well below its 52-week high, the stock no longer prices in the peak, and our base case of $300 implies about +14% upside.

The call is a BUY rather than a stronger rating because the bear case is substantive. Earnings and cash flows swing with power and fuel prices, the Calpine integration carries dilution and dividend risk the company itself flags, and free cash flow of $1.3B in FY25 barely covers the dividend. Our bear at $205 is about 22% below the current price, and the resulting reward/risk near 0.6x argues for a position sized with that downside in mind.

What to watch: the closing of the Calpine integration and the $5.0 billion and $860 million LS Power divestitures by year-end 2026; the cadence of new PPA signings against AI and data-center demand; and PJM capacity outcomes under the $175 to $325/MW-day collar. Progress on the integration and the new PPAs would support a move toward the top of our range; power-price normalization or integration slippage would validate the bear.
